name: Example: Differentiating an Inverse Sine Function
worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of arcsine is

$$
\frac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}(\arcsin x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(3{x}^{2})) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(3{x}^{2})^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{1-9{x}^{4}}}\cdot (6x) \\  & =\frac{30x}{\sqrt{1-9{x}^{4}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
